*I don’t knock. You’re late on rent again, and I’ve warned you twice. The lease gives me access. That’s what I tell myself as I turn the key and let myself into your flat. The air hits me—sweat, coffee, foreign shampoo. Western boy habits. Everything too bold, too careless. Barefoot again. Of course.*

*The lights are off in the kitchen. I can see your laptop glowing on the table, a half-crushed protein bar beside it. A pair of boxer briefs hangs over the back of the couch like a trophy. Pale blue Calvin Klein. Imported. I step around them carefully, heels silent on tile, blouse tucked in too tight for what I’m pretending this visit is about.*

*You’re in the hallway—shirtless. White. Tall. The kind of tall that takes up space Hong Kong doesn’t give. Damp hair. A towel slung low on your hips, drops running down your stomach in clean, foreign lines. You haven’t seen me yet.*

*My mouth opens and closes before I speak. When I do, my voice comes out sharper than I intended.*  
“You were supposed to pay on the first.”

*You turn. Look at me. I forget the next line. I’ve prepared it—something about late fees, something enforceable. But I’m staring at your collarbones. At the rise of your chest. At the small, pale scar on your ribs I’ve never asked about, but memorized.*

*I clear my throat and lift my chin like it’s armor.*  
“You leave the aircon running when you’re not home. You overuse the water heater. And you still haven’t installed the curtain rods I provided. You act like this flat belongs to you.”

*You answer the door in a t-shirt and slacks. The shirt’s half-tucked. Forearms exposed. There’s grey in your beard, but your shoulders are still broad. That part irritates me—how age doesn’t seem to subtract from your presence, only concentrate it.*

*I hand you the envelope without waiting for a greeting. Repair estimates. Padded, of course. You don't even glance at it.*

“You still haven’t paid for the window replacement. And the neighbor downstairs says your shoes make too much noise when you come home late.”

*I say it like I mean it, but my eyes keep drifting. Past your chest. Past your throat. You smell like linen and aftershave and something else—foreign and familiar. The scent of a man who isn't Chinese. A man who was never taught to shrink himself indoors.*

*You lean against the doorframe, one hand braced high, like you own the space. Like you could step forward and I’d be the one backing up. I don’t. I hold my ground, spine straight, heels firm against your tile.*

*“This is a professional visit,” *I say before you can say anything smug.* “I don’t have time for games.”*

*But my voice comes out too smooth. Too quiet. Like I’m not sure who I’m reminding.*
